summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old man with a history of primary central nervous system B-cell lymphoma was admitted for his 28th cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy, along with rituximab and temozolomide. He reported recent dysuria, and a urine culture grew Group B streptococcus, leading to a course of cefdinir. Admission sodium was low at 130, attributed to excessive desmopressin use for urinary frequency; the medication was held initially and restarted at a reduced dose once sodium stabilized. Methotrexate was administered without complications, with appropriate leucovorin rescue and bicarbonate hydration. His CNS lymphoma remains in remission per recent imaging, and he had no seizure activity during admission. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to complete oral leucovorin and sodium bicarbonate, finish antibiotics, and continue temozolomide on a 7-days-on, 7-days-off schedule, with oncology follow-up planned in two to three months.
problems: Primary central nervous system lymphoma, unspecified site, extranodal and solid organ sites
Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Epilepsy, unspecified, without mention of intractable epilepsy
